items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-11-10
items.q: That's when we got Eddie Miller and... Bill Padron. ... Bill Padron stayed with us. He was with the band.

ctx.x: And who was the bass player? Dan LeBlanc, his tuba. Well Dan was a good reader. But not that much.

Yeah, he, you know those tuba players, as you well know, you know. You start to give them a violin sheet, you know, or something like that. It's kind of a little fast one. That's like Jumbo used to tell me. He looked at my part over there when he was playing some of those stuff over there. He says, well, none of these guys around here can play that part. He says, they can't read that fast. I said, well, hell, that's not that fast. I said, after all, they played the trombone over there. You get some fast stuff on…
Well Pinky was with the Owls for quite a while.

items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-10-02
items.q: So Maurice took it. And he happened to get Eddie Miller. So Eddie Miller was the product out of those two bands.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you about these kids that you taught in the Western Union Band. Did any of them grow up to be professionals?

There was a boy, Martyr. He played piano in a couple of places. And to my knowledge, I don't think any of the others did. But then... Maurice took the item band. In fact, the item wanted me to take the band. I said, no. I said, one of them is driving me crazy. I said, I ain't going to get another one. So Maurice took it. And he happened to get Eddie Miller. So Eddie Miller was the product out of those two bands.
Well how did you pronounce Eddie Miller's name then?
